stories.title: Asana clears 5 years of engineering work in 2 weeks using Codex
stories.rationale: Concrete enterprise coding-agent deployment with hard numbers, corroborated by independent analysis.
stories.summary: Asana used OpenAI Codex to replace an outdated testing framework in two weeks, work it estimated would have taken five years, for roughly $12K. The Pragmatic Engineer places this in a broader trend of AI-driven migrations across engineering organizations.

stories.title: Memory prices reportedly up 500% in 12 months
stories.rationale: Directly relevant to AI hardware economics and compute costs; needs primary verification.
stories.summary: Latent.Space reports memory prices have risen roughly 500% over the past year, describing it as Moore's Law effectively reversed to 2007 levels. The trend has significant implications for AI datacenter and hardware costs.

stories.title: Qwen 3.8 27B matches much larger models on intelligence benchmarks
stories.rationale: Notable capability-per-parameter result relevant to open-weight local deployment.
stories.summary: Qwen 3.8 27B, an Apache 2 licensed vision-capable model from Alibaba, scored 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, matching GPT-5.6 Luna and trailing far larger models by one point. Simon Willison notes it is excellent but tends to overthink by default.

stories.title: Agent harnesses, coding-agent workflows, and verification practices
stories.rationale: Core agentic-SDLC content matching reader's stated focus; practitioner analysis.
stories.summary: Latent.Space examines how agent harnesses are being absorbed into model weights, while Simon Willison and Matt Pocock discuss verification-over-line-review practices and planning skills for coding agents. Together they map evolving best practices for agentic software development.

stories.title: AI infra dealmaking: Poolside $12B reverse-execuhire to NVIDIA, Stripe buys OpenRouter
stories.rationale: Major infra/business moves reshaping the model and routing landscape, but secondary newsletter sourcing.
stories.summary: Latent.Space reports NVIDIA's $12B reverse-execuhire of Poolside with a 7GW neocloud buildout, and Stripe's reported $7B acquisition of OpenRouter, alongside NVIDIA pushing customers to build their own models. These reflect consolidation and vertical integration across AI compute, routing, and distribution.

stories.title: Z.ai CEO on GLM-5.3 and a post-training scaling law
stories.rationale: Model-release and scaling-research signal, but via newsletter interview.
stories.summary: Latent.Space covers Z.ai CEO Jie Tang discussing GLM-5.3 and what he frames as a new post-training scaling law beyond parameter count. The discussion touches on shifting emphasis from model size to post-training.

stories.title: Simulation and autonomous AI researchers as an emerging frontier
stories.rationale: Interesting research direction but speculative and secondary-sourced.
stories.summary: Latent.Space and Import AI cover a wave of interest in simulation as a scaling approach and in autonomous AI researchers, including Simile AI's plan to build billions of human digital twins. The pieces frame simulation and recursive self-improvement as the next research frontier.

stories.title: Mojo programming language is now open source
stories.rationale: Relevant systems/AI tooling release with concrete licensing detail.
stories.summary: The Mojo language released its compiler and toolchain under an Apache 2 license, following its 1.0 release. The move fulfills an open-source promise made in 2023, though Mojo's Python-superset goals have since shifted.

stories.title: Hugging Face engineering: inference speedups, agent memory, and GPU utilization
stories.rationale: Practical infra/efficiency techniques with numbers, relevant to deployment costs.
stories.summary: Hugging Face posts cover up to 3.2x faster LFM2.5-DSpark inference, agent memory requirements, a 33-point GPU utilization gain from reordering work, multi-vector embeddings, and ASR benchmark optimization. The collection focuses on efficiency and evaluation for real deployments.

stories.title: Enterprises report large productivity gains from ChatGPT Work (Stampli, NVIDIA)
stories.rationale: Real enterprise adoption stories with numbers, but vendor-authored case studies.
stories.summary: Stampli reported cutting launch production hours by 68% using Codex and ChatGPT Work, while NVIDIA teams described scaling workflows and reducing manual tasks. Both are OpenAI-published customer case studies.
